Wrapping fixed at every width. Two boundary situations to look at:

**1 — A bookmark stuffed with long content.** Open **http://maker:4001/?demo=long**
The top item has an absurdly long title, a long description, a dozen tags, and a long formatted note with a giant link. Check that it stays tidy — text wraps, tags flow onto new lines, nothing spills sideways. Worth glancing at on your **phone** too (this is the phone-comfort point you raised early on).

**2 — A big collection.** Open **http://maker:4001/?demo=many**
This holds 65 bookmarks. Notice the count next to "Saved", and confirm that **search, tag-clicking, and the To read / Finished switch still narrow things instantly** even with a large pile.

Two notes on decisions:
- Long values **wrap and stay readable** rather than being cut off with "…", so you never lose information you saved.
- Each bookmark keeps showing its **saved date**, so as the pile ages you can tell how old something is.

One thing I'll flag honestly: making a *very* large collection (thousands, with smooth scrolling/paging) load fast is a performance matter I'd tune during the build rather than decide here — I've noted it for later.

**Do the long-content and large-collection behaviours look right to you?**
